title: How Leaders Build a Winning Team Culture
summary: A leader's guide to building a winning team culture, including 7 tips for high performance in the workplace.
body_text: How Leaders Build a Winning Team Culture That Drives Lasting Performance Published: 7/14/2026 Table of Contents What Is Team Culture? Why Team Culture Matters: Impact on Performance and Retention The 4 Pillars of a Winning Team Culture How Team Culture Takes Shape Over Time How to Build a Winning Team Culture: 7 Tips Start Building a Winning Team Culture Organizations know that culture matters, but they aren’t always clear on how it’s formed or changed. Team culture builds as a direct result of the daily decisions leaders make about which behaviors they model and reward and which behaviors they choose not to challenge. As those decisions accumulate over time, they inform the team’s culture. When a team works well together, problems surface early and people stay. But when team culture is weak, issues are withheld and talent walks out the door. This post covers what team culture is, why it has a measurable effect on performance and retention, the four elements that define a strong team culture, how culture forms over time, and specific actions leaders can take to build a stronger team environment. Key Takeaways: Team culture is what the majority of people within a team do the majority of the time. Strong team cultures correlate with higher levels of engagement and meaningfully lower turnover across the organization. Leaders shape team culture more than any other single variable, primarily through what they model and what they tolerate. What Is Team Culture? Team culture is what the majority of people on a team do the majority of the time: the shared habits, communication patterns, and norms that define how a team works together in practice, rather than merely in theory. While organizational or workplace culture sets the broader cultural identity of a company, team culture is how that identity actually plays out at the unit level. But the two don’t always match. Two teams within the same organization, operating under the same stated values, can function with entirely different standards around accountability, communication, and conflict, depending on who leads them and how. Team culture shows up not in what a team says it values, but in how people act on those values on a daily basis. Why Team Culture Matters: Impact on Performance and Retention Developing—or perhaps redeveloping—a healthy, organizational culture in today’s environment requires an investment of patience, trust, and support. But the reward is a workforce that shows up authentically, does their very best work, and is less likely to exit when things get tough. — Christi Phillips, Ph.D., co-author of Change: How to Turn Uncertainty Into Opportunity The business case for investing in team culture begins with the high levels of performance on engaged teams. High team engagement typically correlates with positive team cultures, and highly engaged teams consistently outperform their peers on output quality and profitability. Recent research confirms that engagement drives measurable gains in business performance across industries. One study also found that team engagement increases employee retention by more than 20%. The cost of low engagement is equally high: Disengaged employees cost organizations $10 trillion in lost productivity globally in 2025. Manager behavior accounts for 70% of the variance in employee engagement, and it’s ultimately leaders who shape culture and create the conditions for team engagement to flourish. Positive team cultures also expand the range of solutions a team generates. When team members trust that honest effort, even when it fails, will prompt a learning conversation, they experiment more readily. That willingness leads to better solutions, faster. The 4 Pillars of a Winning Team Culture FranklinCovey research on organizational effectiveness points to four interlocking dimensions that, when developed together, build a thriving workplace culture : trust, accountability, agility, and feedback. 1. Trust Trust is what enables leaders and teams to communicate clearly and move with confidence, reducing operational friction and driving ongoing innovation. Teams with high trust are also able to recover from setbacks faster than teams where trust is low or fragile. Building a high-trust team culture requires leaders to demonstrate empathy and consistency over time. Team members who feel heard and valued contribute more fully to shared work and take the interpersonal risks that genuine collaboration requires. Trust accumulates when leaders follow through on commitments and share information openly with the team. Treating people with genuine care during difficult periods deepens that foundation further. 2. Accountability When leaders model and help their teams build accountability in the workplace , they establish shared standards and empower their teams to take responsibility for outcomes, follow through on commitments, and feel a purposeful connection to their work. The distinction between accountability and blame is key. Accountability focuses on outcomes and learning, while blame focuses on assigning fault. Team cultures where the two blur tend to produce self-protective behavior. But when leaders openly “own” their mistakes, set clear expectations, and address performance gaps quickly, accountability becomes an essential element of team culture that removes fear and confusion from the equation. 3. Agility Agile teams adapt to changing conditions without losing momentum or cohesion. They process new information quickly and adjust course when circumstances shift. Leaders cultivate their ability to lead through uncertainty by modeling comfort with ambiguity and acknowledging when a plan needs to change and why. Teams that observe their leaders freeze or overreact under pressure tend to develop the same response. Agile leaders help their teams pair adaptability with clear priorities, so they can move quickly and stay aligned. Team cultures that develop both are better equipped to sustain performance as conditions change. 4. Feedback Feedback-rich cultures grow faster than feedback-scarce ones. When team members receive specific, actionable input on their work, they course-correct quickly and develop their capabilities over time. Successful leaders also solicit feedback on their own performance. When leaders ask for feedback and respond to it visibly, they signal that feedback flows in all directions and is safe to give. Using feedback as fuel , rather than treating it as a negative force, is one of the practices that separates team cultures with strong learning environments from those that plateau. Download our guide, The 4 Pillars of a Thriving Workplace Culture , to multiply performance and create a culture where people want to stay. How Team Culture Takes Shape Over Time Team culture accumulates from individual interactions over time; in many organizations, this accumulation often occurs without an intentional plan or execution. In the initial formation phase, the first interactions within a team set a tone that proves surprisingly durable. Early norms around how the team handles conflict and raises problems tend to persist long after individuals leave the team or organization. The patterns leaders establish in a team’s first weeks carry more weight than most recognize. Through repetition, informal habits harden into norms. Norms, once set, define how the team operates, and new team members absorb them by observation. A new hire learns the real team culture by watching how the team responds when something goes wrong or when pressure starts to build. The leader’s role throughout this process is both active and consequential. Every interaction either reinforces or corrects the team culture built by the group. Leaders who are intentional about the signals they send in the small moments build a stronger culture through consistency than through any single initiative. How to Build a Winning Team Culture: 7 Steps Building team culture is daily work. Large periodic initiatives matter less than the cumulative effect of how leaders show up in ordinary moments. That means that the strongest cultural lifts happen through small, repeated behaviors. Here are seven practical approaches for building a winning team culture . 1. Define and Revisit Shared Values Leaders keep team culture values relevant by reinforcing them in the daily discussions they have and in the feedback they give. A values conversation means more when it connects to a specific situation the team is currently facing. 2. Hold Weekly 1-on-1s These conversations convert team culture from something intangible into a lived relationship, giving leaders consistent visibility into what is working and what needs attention. Leveraging 1-on-1s ranks among the highest-leverage behaviors available to managers who want to strengthen team culture at the individual level. Download our guide, 100+ Questions for Better 1-on-1s With Your Direct Reports , to uncover opportunities for employee development, problem solving, and relationship building. 3. Make Trust Observable To visibly build trust, leaders may open meetings by asking, “What’s not working?” and immediately acknowledge the person who names the problem first. This teaches the team that candid input is valued and translates the intent to build trust into a sustainable practice. Other trust-building behaviors include modeling transparency, communicating expectations clearly, and practicing active listening. 4. Demonstrate Accountability Publicly Teams closely observe how a leader responds when something goes wrong. When that response is repeated consistently, it becomes the norm for how everyone handles setbacks. When leaders own their mistakes openly and follow through on stated commitments, they establish the accountability standard for the entire team. Take the first step toward building a high-trust culture when you download our guide, 6 Key Communication Phrases to Build Trust and Inspire Your Team . 5. Build Recognition Into a Regular Cadence To build a winning culture, leaders must make recognition a consistent habit. When leaders name specific behaviors that reflect shared values, they reinforce the team culture; in other words, what gets recognized is repeated. This can be as simple as calling out a win in a weekly meeting or a contribution in a shared channel, provided it connects to the values the team is trying to reinforce. Of course, bigger expressions of recognition are also crucial for promoting employee engagement and job satisfaction, as well as a healthy workplace culture. 6. Address Misalignment Quickly When leaders allow behaviors that contradict the team’s stated values or norms to go unchallenged, those exceptions harden into the actual team culture. The faster a leader names the gap between stated values and actual behavior, the lower the cost to the team’s culture. Waiting for a problem to fix itself introduces confusion and drains team energy; being clear is being kind, so don’t avoid having a difficult conversation due to discomfort. Learn four strategies to tackle tension with confidence when you download our guide, Navigating Difficult Conversations . 7. Measure Culture With Regularity Pulse surveys and skip-level discussions reveal what annual engagement surveys are too infrequent to catch. Regular measurement signals that team culture is a priority, not a background condition. Start Building a Winning Team Culture Team culture is the product of what leaders do consistently, in ordinary moments, over time. The leaders who see the strongest results continue to build team culture as a daily commitment—strengthening trust, accountability, agility, and feedback in ways that build an environment where people perform at their best and choose to stay. Move from insight to action and learn how FranklinCovey empowers organizations to build a winning culture where people and performance thrive.

title: Cosmic Rundown: Shadcn Goes Base UI, EU Chat Control, and Organic Maps
summary: Shadcn/UI switches from Radix to Base UI. EU Chat Control advances through fast-track. Organic Maps trends as a privacy-first navigation option. Plus web crypto skepticism, compiler resources, and solar-powered railways.
body_text: Shadcn/UI Defaults to Base UI Shadcn/UI, the component library that changed how developers think about copy-paste UI, now defaults to Base UI instead of Radix . The Hacker News discussion is exploring what this means for existing projects and the broader React component ecosystem. Base UI, maintained by the MUI team, offers unstyled, accessible components similar to Radix but with different architectural decisions. For teams heavily invested in Shadcn components, the migration path matters. The changelog indicates backward compatibility, but production codebases will want to test thoroughly before upgrading. This shift reflects ongoing consolidation in the headless component space. Competition between Radix, Base UI, and other primitives libraries benefits developers through improved APIs and better accessibility defaults. EU Chat Control Advances The EU Council forced Chat Control through fast-track procedures , according to Heise. The HN thread covers the technical implications for end-to-end encryption and what this means for messaging platforms operating in Europe. The regulation requires messenger services to scan communications for illegal content. Critics argue this fundamentally undermines encryption. Supporters claim it can be implemented without breaking E2E encryption, though security researchers remain skeptical. For developers building communication features, understanding the evolving European regulatory landscape is increasingly important. Compliance requirements may affect architecture decisions for apps serving EU users. Organic Maps Gains Traction Organic Maps , an open-source, privacy-focused navigation app, is trending in the HN discussion . Built on OpenStreetMap data, it works offline and doesn't track users. The project represents a growing interest in privacy-respecting alternatives to Google Maps. For teams building location features, OpenStreetMap-based solutions offer an interesting alternative to commercial APIs, especially for privacy-conscious user bases. Web Cryptography Skepticism A post arguing that web-based cryptography is always snake oil sparked significant debate . The core argument: browser-based crypto can't provide the security guarantees users expect because the server delivering the JavaScript could be compromised. The counterargument in the thread: threat models vary, and web crypto serves legitimate use cases even if it can't match native application security. For teams implementing client-side encryption, understanding these tradeoffs is essential. Compilers and Language Design A free textbook on Introduction to Compilers and Language Design is circulating in the HN discussion . The resource covers lexical analysis through code generation with practical examples. Compiler knowledge increasingly matters for frontend developers. Understanding how tools like Babel, TypeScript, and bundlers work under the hood helps debug complex build issues and optimize output. Quick Hits KiCad in the browser : A Show HN demo brings the PCB design tool to the web. The discussion covers WASM performance and use cases for browser-based hardware design. Rayfish VPN : A new peer-to-peer mesh VPN claims to operate without a central server to trust. The thread examines the architecture and security implications. Fast Software essay resurfaces : Craig Mod's 2019 piece on fast software being the best software is getting renewed attention . Performance remains a feature. GNU Emacs architecture : A PDF deep-dive into Emacs internals is making rounds in the discussion . Understanding long-lived software architectures offers lessons for modern systems. Solar rail in Europe : Following successful Swiss trials, solar-powered railways may expand across Europe. Infrastructure innovation continues outside traditional tech sectors. What This Means for Content Teams The Shadcn/UI shift illustrates how quickly frontend tooling evolves. Component libraries that seemed stable can change foundations overnight. For teams building content-heavy applications, having a CMS that stays flexible regardless of frontend framework changes matters. The Chat Control discussion highlights ongoing tension between regulation and technical architecture. Content platforms operating internationally need infrastructure that can adapt to varying compliance requirements without rebuilding core systems. title: EOR: qué es, cómo funciona y cuánto cuesta
summary: EOR significa employer of record: emplea a tu equipo en otro país sin abrir entidad. Ve cómo funciona, qué cuesta y en qué se diferencia de un PEO.
body_text: Si quieres contratar a alguien en un país donde tu empresa no tiene una entidad legal, un EOR (Employer of Record, o empleador de registro) suele ser la forma más rápida y cumplida de hacerlo. Un EOR es un tercero que se convierte en el empleador legal de tu trabajador, gestionando nómina, impuestos, beneficios y cumplimiento local, mientras esa persona trabaja para ti en el día a día. Esta guía explica qué significa EOR, cómo funciona, cuánto cuesta y cuándo conviene usarlo. Ontop es una plataforma global de nómina y pagos que permite a las empresas contratar y pagar equipos en más de 150 países , así que el cumplimiento y los pagos de emplear en el exterior quedan resueltos en un solo lugar. Puntos clave EOR significa Employer of Record: una empresa que emplea legalmente a tus trabajadores en tu nombre en un país donde no tienes entidad. El EOR gestiona nómina, retención de impuestos, beneficios, contratos y cumplimiento laboral local; tú diriges el trabajo diario. Permite contratar en el exterior en días, en lugar de los meses que toma abrir una entidad local. Es distinto de un PEO (coempleo dentro de tu propia entidad) y de contratar a un contratista independiente (sin relación laboral). El precio suele ser una tarifa mensual fija por empleado o un porcentaje del salario. ¿Qué significa EOR? EOR significa Employer of Record, o empleador de registro. Es una empresa especializada que asume la responsabilidad legal y administrativa de ser el empleador oficial de tus trabajadores, casi siempre en un país extranjero. El EOR se convierte en el empleador legal, mientras el trabajador reporta a tu empresa y es dirigido por ella. Es el mecanismo estándar para emplear personas en el exterior sin abrir una filial. ¿Qué hace un EOR? El EOR carga con las responsabilidades del empleador para que tú no tengas que asumirlas localmente. En la práctica: Redacta contratos laborales que cumplen la ley local. Corre la nómina y retiene impuestos y aportes de seguridad social. Administra beneficios legales y complementarios. Mantiene la relación laboral conforme a la legislación local. Gestiona desvinculaciones e indemnizaciones según las reglas del país. ¿Cómo funciona un EOR? El flujo es sencillo. Eliges a la persona que quieres contratar y acuerdan el rol y el pago. El EOR firma un contrato laboral cumplido con esa persona y se convierte formalmente en su empleador legal. Tú diriges su trabajo diario como con cualquier miembro del equipo, mientras el EOR corre la nómina, remite los impuestos y administra los beneficios en segundo plano. Cada mes fondeas al EOR y este paga al trabajador en su moneda local. EOR vs PEO vs contratista Estos tres modelos se confunden a menudo, pero implican niveles muy distintos de riesgo y control: Modelo Empleador legal ¿Necesita entidad local? Ideal para Employer of record (EOR) El EOR No Contratar empleados en el exterior rápido y cumplido PEO Tu empresa (coempleo) Sí Externalizar RR. HH. donde ya tienes entidad Contratista independiente Ninguno (autónomo) No Trabajo por proyecto, no roles permanentes ¿Cuándo conviene usar un EOR? Un EOR tiene sentido cuando quieres contratar a un empleado en un país donde no tienes entidad, cuando necesitas a alguien trabajando en semanas y no en meses, cuando pruebas un nuevo mercado antes de abrir una filial, o cuando la ley laboral local es tan compleja que un error de cumplimiento saldría caro. Si el trabajo es realmente por proyecto e independiente, quizá encaje mejor un contratista , cuidando siempre la clasificación. ¿Cuánto cuesta un EOR? Los proveedores de EOR suelen cobrar una tarifa mensual fija por empleado o un porcentaje del salario, además de los costos reales de nómina y aportes. El valor está en lo que evitas: el tiempo y el gasto de constituir una entidad, mantenerla y contratar experiencia legal y de RR. HH. local. Preguntas frecuentes ¿Qué significa EOR? Employer of Record, una empresa que emplea legalmente a trabajadores en tu nombre en un país determinado. ¿Es lo mismo un EOR que una agencia de empleo? No. Una agencia busca y provee personal; un EOR se convierte en el empleador legal de las personas que tú ya elegiste, gestionando nómina y cumplimiento. ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre un EOR y un PEO? El EOR es el empleador legal completo y no requiere que tengas entidad local. El PEO coemplea dentro de tu entidad existente, así que sí necesitas una. ¿Qué tan rápido puede contratar un EOR en el exterior? A menudo en días, frente a los meses que puede tomar abrir y registrar una entidad local. Conclusión El EOR es la respuesta más simple a una pregunta difícil: ¿cómo contratar a un empleado real en un país donde no estás constituido como empleador? El EOR carga con el peso legal y de cumplimiento, tú conservas la relación de trabajo, y la persona recibe un contrato cumplido y un pago confiable. title: What Your Employee’s UAN Number Reveals About Their Real Work History
summary: Discover how UAN verification helps employers instantly check candidate employment history and easily catch fake experience claims.
body_text: Insights & Resources What Your Employee’s UAN Number Reveals About Their Real Work History July 30, 2026 Shashank Yadav No comments yet Most Indian employers have heard of the UAN. They know it has something to do with provident fund and that employees need it for PF withdrawals and transfers. What most employers do not realize is that the UAN is one of the most powerful hiring tools available to them, and it is hiding in plain sight. The Universal Account Number is not just a PF identifier. It is a verified, government maintained record of every formal employer a person has ever worked for. Every company that contributed PF on behalf of an employee is logged in the EPFO database against that UAN, along with dates of joining, dates of leaving, member IDs, and contribution status. This means that when a candidate tells you they spent three years at a reputed company, you can verify that claim in minutes. Not by calling their former HR department and hoping someone picks up. Not by inspecting an experience certificate that could have been printed from a template. But by checking the actual EPFO database, which records real monetary contributions made by real employers. If the employer actually contributed PF for this person during the claimed period, the record will be there. If they did not, it will not be. No story, no forged letter, and no rehearsed interview answer can change what the database shows. Why Employment Claims Are the Hardest Thing to Verify Traditionally Of all the things a candidate can lie about, employment history is the hardest to catch through traditional methods. Here is why. Education fraud is relatively straightforward to detect. You contact the university, they check their records, and they confirm whether the degree was issued. Criminal records can be searched through court databases. Address verification can be done through field visits or digital checks. But verifying employment history traditionally requires calling the candidate’s previous employer’s HR department and asking them to confirm dates, designation, and reason for leaving. This sounds simple in theory. In practice, it is a nightmare. Many companies, especially large ones, have policies that restrict what HR can share with external callers. They will confirm that the person worked there and provide dates of employment, but nothing more. No performance details, no reason for leaving, no information about whether the person was a star performer or a walking liability. Small companies are even harder. The “HR department” might be a single person who handles everything from payroll to office supplies. They may not respond to calls or emails from unknown numbers. The company may have shut down entirely. The person listed as the reference might be a friend of the candidate who agreed to play the role. And then there are the candidates who create entirely fictional employers. In an era where anyone can register a domain name, set up a professional looking website, and print letterhead, fabricating a previous employer is disturbingly easy. This is where UAN verification changes the game completely. How UAN Verification Works and What It Shows Every employee in India who earns up to Rs 15,000 per month (the current wage ceiling for mandatory PF) receives PF contributions from their employer. This contribution is recorded under the employee’s UAN in the EPFO database. Over time, the UAN accumulates a complete employment trail. When you verify a candidate’s UAN through a platform like ID Verify by SalaryBox, the EPFO database returns a set of information that is remarkably detailed. You see the employee’s name as registered with EPFO, which you can immediately compare against the name they gave you during the application process. A mismatch here is a significant red flag because EPFO names are verified during KYC linking. You see a list of all employers who have contributed PF for this person, identified by their establishment IDs and names. Each employer entry includes the date the employee joined and the date they left (if applicable). This gives you a complete timeline of their formal employment history. You see whether each employment record is active or inactive, which tells you whether the person is still receiving PF contributions from a current employer. If they are applying for a job with you while still actively employed somewhere else and did not disclose it, the UAN will reveal it. You also see the KYC status, which indicates whether the employee has linked their Aadhaar, PAN, and bank account to their UAN. A fully KYC compliant UAN adds another layer of identity validation. Six Things UAN Verification Catches That Interviews Cannot Fabricated employment history This is the most straightforward catch. A candidate says they worked at Company X for three years. You check their UAN. No PF contributions from Company X appear anywhere in the record. The employment was either completely fabricated, or they worked there on a cash basis with no formal employment relationship, which contradicts the “senior role” they described in the interview. Inflated tenure A candidate claims five years at a company, but the UAN shows PF contributions from that company spanning only two years and three months. They did work there, but they significantly exaggerated how long. This is one of the most common forms of resume fraud because candidates assume nobody will verify the exact dates. Concealed employers Sometimes the interesting thing is not what the UAN confirms but what it reveals that the candidate did not mention. If their resume shows three employers over the past eight years, but the UAN shows PF contributions from five different companies during that period, there are two employers the candidate chose to hide. Why? Usually because they were terminated, or their tenure was embarrassingly short, or something happened that they do not want you to know about. Dual employment The UAN can show overlapping employment periods. If PF contributions were being made by two different employers during the same months, the person was either working two jobs simultaneously, or something unusual was going on with their PF records. Either way, it warrants a conversation. Misrepresented job level While the UAN does not directly show job titles, it reveals the size and type of establishment through the employer’s registered name and ID. If a candidate claims they were a “Regional Manager” at a company, but the UAN shows that the establishment is a small proprietorship with fewer than 20 employees, the “regional” part of that title deserves questioning. No formal employment despite claims Some candidates claim years of experience but have never been in a formal employment relationship. Their UAN either does not exist, or it was created recently with no contribution history. This is particularly telling when the candidate has described roles that would certainly have PF contributions, such as working at a retail chain, a hospital, or a manufacturing plant. When UAN Verification Is Most Valuable Not every hire requires the same level of scrutiny. UAN verification is most valuable in specific situations. When hiring for roles that require genuine experience. If you are hiring an accountant, a store manager, a nurse, or a machine operator, the candidate’s claimed experience directly affects whether they can do the job safely and competently. UAN verification confirms whether that experience is real. When the candidate’s resume seems too good to be true. A candidate with a perfectly linear career progression, all at well known companies, with no gaps and steadily increasing responsibilities, might be the real deal. Or they might have crafted a fiction. UAN verification settles the question quickly. When you are hiring someone who will handle money, inventory, or sensitive data. People in positions of trust need verified backgrounds. If a candidate claims three years as an accounts executive and the UAN shows nothing from that employer, you do not want this person anywhere near your finances. When you are hiring at a level where checking references is impractical. Many small business owners do not have the time, experience, or confidence to conduct professional reference checks. UAN verification provides much of the same information automatically, without the awkward phone calls and uncertain reliability of spoken references. When hiring in high turnover industries. Retail, hospitality, logistics, and healthcare see frequent job changes. Candidates in these sectors may have worked at five or six employers in the past few years. Manually verifying each one would take weeks. UAN verification shows the entire trail in minutes. How to Use UAN Verification in Your Hiring Process Making UAN verification part of your hiring workflow is straightforward. During the interview or application stage, ask the candidate for their UAN along with other identity details like PAN and Voter ID. Most formally employed candidates know their UAN because they have used it for PF balance checks, withdrawals, or transfers. If a candidate says they do not have a UAN, pay attention to the context. A genuine fresher straight out of college or ITI will not have one, and that is perfectly normal. But a candidate claiming five years of experience at formal employers should have a UAN. If they say they do not, ask why. The answer will either be reasonable (they worked entirely in cash based roles) or suspicious (they are trying to avoid having their employment claims checked). Run the UAN check alongside PAN, Voter ID, and DL checks through ID Verify by SalaryBox. The platform processes all four checks in a single flow, so you are not adding extra steps. You are simply getting a richer picture of the candidate in the same ten minutes. When the results come back, compare the employment timeline from the UAN against the resume or what the candidate told you in the interview. Look for matches, gaps, and contradictions. If the candidate claimed experience at three companies and the UAN confirms PF contributions from all three during the stated periods, you have strong corroboration. If the UAN tells a different story, you have a conversation to have before you make an offer. UAN Verification Plus Identity Checks Equals Confidence UAN verification is powerful on its own, but it becomes even more valuable when combined with the other checks available through ID Verify. PAN verification confirms the candidate’s legal identity and tax registration. This is your foundation. If the PAN does not match the candidate’s stated name, nothing else matters. Voter ID verification provides an independent identity cross reference from the Election Commission, including address confirmation. Driving Licence verification confirms licence validity and vehicle class authorization, which is critical for any role involving driving. UAN verification adds the employment history dimension, turning a set of identity checks into a comprehensive candidate profile. When all four checks agree, when the name on the PAN matches the name on the Voter ID, the DL is active and valid, and the UAN confirms the claimed employment history, you have a level of confidence in the candidate that no interview or reference check can match. When any of these checks disagree with each other or with what the candidate told you, you have caught something that could have cost you lakhs. How ID Verify by SalaryBox Makes This Effortless ID Verify puts PAN, Voter ID, DL, and UAN verification into a single candidate flow. You enter the details once, select the checks you want, and get results in minutes. The platform handles the government database queries. It handles the cross record comparison. It handles the report generation. You review clear, structured results and make your hiring decision with actual data instead of assumptions. Every verification produces a downloadable PDF report. This is your documentation. Your compliance record. Your proof of due diligence. It goes into the candidate’s file and stays there. There are no subscriptions, no minimum volumes, and no setup fees. You pay for the checks you run. A single four check verification costs under Rs 500. Stop guessing about work experience. Start checking it. Verify your next candidate at verify.salarybox.in Frequently Asked Questions Can HR at a previous company see that I checked a candidate’s UAN? No. UAN verification through authorized platforms queries the EPFO database. It does not notify the candidate’s current or previous employer. The check is confidential between you and the verification platform. What if the candidate worked at a company that did not pay PF? Some small employers do not contribute PF, either because they fall below the employee threshold or because they operate informally. In such cases, the UAN will not show contributions from that employer. This does not necessarily mean the candidate lied, but it does mean you cannot independently verify that particular employment claim through UAN. You may need to follow up with a direct reference check for that specific employer. Can candidates manipulate their UAN records? No. UAN records are maintained by EPFO and reflect actual monetary contributions made by employers. An employee cannot add, remove, or alter employer entries in their UAN record. This is what makes UAN verification so reliable. It is based on money that actually changed hands, not documents that can be fabricated. What if the candidate is a freelancer or worked on contract? Freelancers and independent contractors typically do not have PF contributions because they are not classified as employees. If a candidate tells you they freelanced for three years and their UAN shows no contributions during that period, it is consistent with their story. UAN verification is most useful for verifying claims of formal, salaried employment. Do I need the candidate’s permission to check their UAN? Yes. Under the DPDP Act 2023, you must obtain written consent from the candidate before processing their personal data, which includes running verification checks. A simple consent form explaining which checks will be conducted is sufficient. How far back does UAN history go? UAN was introduced in 2014. For employment before that, EPFO records may be linked through older member IDs, but coverage is less comprehensive. For any employment from 2014 onwards at a PF registered establishment, UAN records are generally reliable and complete. Related Shashank Yadav Leave a Reply Cancel reply

body_text: View All News Edgewise Therapeutics Reports Inducement Grants as permitted by the Nasdaq Listing Rules July 1, 2026 BOULDER, Colo. , July 1, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Edgewise Therapeutics, Inc. ("Edgewise" or the "Company"), (Nasdaq: EWTX), a leading muscle disease biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics for muscular dystrophies and serious cardiac conditions, today announced that on June 30, 2026, Edgewise granted inducement stock options to purchase a total of 16,500 shares of Edgewise's common stock to 2 new non-executive employees in connection with the commencement of their employment, pursuant to Edgewise's 2024 Inducement Equity Incentive Plan (the "Inducement Plan"). Each inducement stock option has an exercise price of $40.63 per share, which is equal to the closing price of a share of Edgewise common stock on the grant date, and shall vest as follows: 25% of the shares subject to such inducement stock option shall vest on the one year anniversary of the start date of each employee, and an additional one forty-eighth (1/48th) of the shares subject to such inducement stock option shall vest monthly thereafter, subject to the employee's continued service. Each inducement award is subject to the terms of the Inducement Plan and related forms of agreements, and were granted as inducements material to these employees to enter into employment with Edgewise in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). About Edgewise Therapeutics Edgewise Therapeutics is a leading muscle disease biopharmaceutical company developing novel therapeutics for muscular dystrophies and serious cardiac conditions. The Company's deep expertise in muscle physiology is driving a new generation of novel therapeutics. Sevasemten is an orally administered first-in-class fast skeletal myosin inhibitor in late-stage clinical trials in Becker and Duchenne muscular dystrophies. EDG-7500 is a novel cardiac sarcomere modulator for the treatment of symptomatic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, currently in Phase 2 clinical development. EDG-15400 is a novel cardiac sarcomere modulator for the treatment of heart failure, currently in Phase 1 clinical development. The entire team at Edgewise is dedicated to our mission: changing the lives of patients and families affected by serious muscle diseases. title: How to use AI to create better docs
summary: Improving an entire doc, just a part, summarising or translating it - it's all possible with AI and in this article you'll learn how.
body_text: At Slite, we have a tradition of hosting monthly Office Hours sessions . During these events, we gather online with some of our customers, chat about new features and our roadmap, and explore a specific knowledge management topic. Last time, we had a great discussion on how you can use AI to create even better documentation. If you're curious you can check out the entire session here, or read on to learn our takeaways on creating amazing documentation your team actually consumes, by leveraging AI: ‍ During this month's session, when asking the audience if they use AI for their writing, most mentioned that they recently starting to use it. The most common use cases included: Summarising documents Improving spelling and grammar In general improving documents And in some cases, using generative AI as a starting point (but never the final product!) While AI is often seen as a magic solution, we quickly agreed during our chat that fully relying on AI might not be the best choice for creating content (for your knowledge base). At Slite, we also truly believe that the best content comes directly from you. When you're building a knowledge base for your team, it should be packed with highly specific details—details that are unique to your company, product, customers, and ways of working. You can ask ChatGPT to sketch out a step-by-step plan for onboarding a new customer, and while that might be a fantastic starting point for crafting an onboarding process, it's not something we should pop directly into our knowledge base. In your company wiki, you want to be super specific, documenting every step you should take, adding extra details where mistakes commonly happen, and capturing lessons learned along the way. So for a knowledge base we still highly recommend that you sit down and do the initial work yourself. That being said, AI can be your trusty sidekick, and help you to get your message across in a clearer, improved and better formatted way. By just a click of a button. So let's dive into the ways Slite AI can help you to improve your docs! Improve entire docs By using the "Improve" button at the right-side of your document, you can improve your document as a whole in a helpful side by side view. You have the option to improve the formatting, make it shorter, translate, or change the tone of voice. Or, even do multiple things at the same time! Improve parts of docs Similar to the above, you can also use Slite AI on a section of your doc. To do so, highlight the part of your doc you would like to improve, click the "Improve" button from the in-context menu, and either select one of the default prompts, or create your own prompt. And when we say create your own prompt, we mean it, the sky is the limit! Just make sure it serves your audience. Translate If you click on the three dots in the top right corner of your doc, you'll open op the doc menu. One of the options you can find here is "Translate". This gives you the option to instantly translate your docs in multiple different languages. You can either translate and read, as sometimes it can be easier to read about a complex policy in your native language, or save multiple versions of the document in different languages. Ask on the doc level Pro-tip from one of our customers! Once you have your first draft ready, you can use Ask to be your proof reader. Instead of opening our global Ask, you can limit Ask to your current doc only by clicking on the hand icon on the right-side of your doc. Here you can ask some key questions about your doc, and see if Ask is able to answer these questions correctly. If the answers are correct, congrats! You have likely drafted a comprehensive doc. If Ask misses out on some key elements, it is likely that your actual audience will do the same. It can give you some pointers on which content to improve or expand upon. Summarise And lastly, just before your doc is ready to be shared, you can add a short summary at the top of the document. Just hit "/" in the editor and select "Summarize doc". This will add in an AI generated summary of your doc which can greatly help your audience to consume your content. This article was written by Anouk, with the help of the "Fix spelling and grammar" and "Change tone" prompts from Slite AI. ‍

title: Pet-Inclusive Weddings: How to Include Your Dog (or Cat) in Your Big Day
summary: Quick answer: To include your pet in your wedding, start by confirming your venue allows animals, then assign a dedicated pet handler for the day.
body_text: Last Updated on July 21, 2026 by Joy Editors Quick answer: To include your pet in your wedding, start by confirming your venue allows animals, then assign a dedicated pet handler for the day. Most couples include dogs in the ceremony as ring bearers or walk-down companions, then have the handler take the pet home before the reception. Plan logistics early: temperament check, vet visit, rehearsal with the pet, and a backup plan if your pet gets overwhelmed. More couples are including their pets in weddings than ever before. Dogs walk down the aisle as ring bearers, cats make cameo appearances in getting-ready photos, and some couples build their entire venue search around pet-friendliness. But pulling it off smoothly requires real planning: not every venue allows animals, not every pet handles crowds well, and not every wedding timeline works with a four-legged guest. This guide covers everything you need to know to include your pet in your wedding, from venue logistics to day-of handling to the backup plan you should have ready. Is a Pet-Inclusive Wedding Right for You? Before diving into logistics, honestly assess whether including your pet is the right call. Consider: Temperament: Is your pet comfortable around large groups of people, loud music, and unfamiliar environments? A dog that gets anxious at the park may not thrive at a 150-person wedding. The timeline: Most pets do best for a short window (30 to 60 minutes). Plan their appearance for a specific moment, not the entire day. Guest comfort: Some guests have allergies or fear of animals. A pet-friendly wedding should accommodate everyone. Venue restrictions: Many venues prohibit animals entirely. This needs to be confirmed before you book. If your pet is social, calm in new environments, and you have someone who can handle them, including them in the wedding can be one of the most memorable and photographed moments of the day. How to Find a Pet-Friendly Wedding Venue Not all venues that say “pet-friendly” mean it the same way. Some allow pets outdoors only. Others require a pet deposit or insurance rider. A few welcome animals everywhere on the property. When evaluating venues, ask: Are pets allowed during the ceremony, the reception, or both? Are there breed or size restrictions? Is there a pet deposit or additional fee? Are there designated outdoor areas where pets can take breaks? Does the venue require proof of vaccinations or a pet liability waiver? Outdoor venues (gardens, farms, estates, beaches) tend to be more accommodating than indoor ballrooms or historic buildings. If your venue does not allow pets during the event, some couples arrange for the pet to appear for photos only, before guests arrive. When you find a venue that works, share all the details on your wedding website so guests know what to expect. If pets will be present during the ceremony, a brief note on your website helps guests with allergies or concerns plan accordingly. Roles Your Pet Can Play The most common ways to include pets in weddings: Role How it works Best for Ring bearer Pet walks down the aisle with rings attached to collar or a small pillow on their back Well-trained dogs comfortable on leash in crowds Aisle escort Pet walks with the bride, groom, or a member of the wedding party Any calm, leash-trained dog Flower dog Pet wears a floral collar or pulls a small wagon of petals Medium to large dogs who tolerate accessories Photo guest Pet appears for pre-ceremony or couple portraits only Any pet, including cats (easier to control in a brief setting) Guest of honor Pet sits with a handler in a front-row seat during the ceremony Calm, quiet dogs Cocktail hour companion Pet mingles with guests during cocktail hour, departs before dinner Social, friendly dogs who enjoy attention The Pet Handler: Your Most Important Hire A dedicated pet handler is non-negotiable. This is someone whose only job is managing your pet from arrival to departure. They are not a bridesmaid doubling as a dog-sitter. They are not a groomsman who “does not mind.” They are a person with one responsibility: your pet. Options for pet handlers: Professional pet attendant: Some pet-sitting services specialize in wedding day care. They handle transport, grooming touch-ups, feeding, bathroom breaks, and departure. Cost: $150 to $500 depending on hours and location. Trusted friend or family member: Someone who knows your pet, is not in the wedding party, and is genuinely willing to leave the ceremony early if needed. Dog walker or pet sitter you already use: Your pet already trusts them, which reduces anxiety. The handler should attend the rehearsal with the pet, know the exit plan, and have your vet’s number saved. Planning the Day-of Timeline for Your Pet Most pets should be on-site for 1 to 2 hours maximum. Build a specific timeline: Sample pet timeline: 2 hours before ceremony: Pet arrives with handler. Walk, bathroom break, settle in. 30 minutes before: Getting-ready photos with pet (if desired). Ceremony: Pet walks down the aisle or sits with handler in front row. Immediately after ceremony: Couple + pet photos (10 to 15 minutes). Before cocktail hour: Handler takes pet home or to boarding. Pet’s job is done. This keeps your pet’s time short, reduces stress, and avoids the chaos of a dog at a crowded reception with loud music and food everywhere. Share the full wedding schedule, including when the pet will be present, on your wedding website so guests and vendors know the plan. What to Pack for Your Pet Create a pet day-of kit: Leash and collar (plus a backup) Water bowl and water Treats (high-value, for bribery during photos) Poop bags A towel or blanket for resting Any calming aids your vet recommends (not sedatives unless prescribed) A lint roller for post-cuddle wardrobe emergencies The pet’s outfit or accessories (floral collar, bow tie, bandana) Pet Attire and Accessories Keep it comfortable. Your pet should be able to move, breathe, and see normally in whatever they wear. Popular options: Floral collar or garland: Coordinate with your florist. Use pet-safe flowers only (avoid lilies, baby’s breath, and chrysanthemums, which are toxic to dogs and cats). Bow tie or bandana: Simple, lightweight, easy to remove if the pet gets uncomfortable. Custom leash: Personalized with the couple’s names or “Best Dog” for photos. “Ring bearer” sign: A small sign attached to the collar or carried by the handler. Test any outfit or accessory at home before the wedding. If your pet tries to remove it within 5 minutes, it is not going to work on the day. Rehearsal with Your Pet If your pet has a role in the ceremony, a rehearsal is essential. Bring them to the rehearsal (or visit the venue beforehand) so they can: Get familiar with the space, sounds, and surfaces Practice walking down the aisle on leash Meet the handler in the venue environment Identify any triggers (slippery floors, loud echoes, other animals nearby) Even calm, well-trained dogs can behave differently in an unfamiliar setting. A rehearsal gives you time to adjust the plan if needed. The Backup Plan Every pet-inclusive wedding needs an exit strategy. Things that can go wrong: Your pet gets anxious, barks during vows, or refuses to walk Weather changes force the ceremony indoors (where pets may not be allowed) A guest has a severe allergy you did not know about Your pet has an accident on the venue floor The backup plan is simple: the handler removes the pet calmly and quietly. No drama, no disruption. This is why the handler must be dedicated to this one role. Have the handler’s car nearby, packed with the pet kit, ready for an early departure at any point. Including Pets You Cannot Bring to the Venue If your venue does not allow animals, or your pet is not suited for crowds, you can still honor them: Photo charm: Attach a small photo of your pet to your bouquet or boutonniere. Signature cocktail: Name a drink after your pet. Table cards: Feature your pet’s photo on escort cards or table numbers. Cake topper: A custom cake topper that includes your pet. Wedding website feature: Add a section about your pet on your wedding website , with a photo and a fun bio. Guests love it. Guest Communication Let guests know in advance that a pet will be present. This is both a courtesy (allergies, phobias) and a way to build excitement. Your RSVP questions can include a note about pets being present, and your wedding website is the best place to share the details: which events the pet will attend, how long they will be present, and that a handler is managing them. For guests with allergies, knowing the pet will only be present for the outdoor ceremony (and not the indoor reception) can make the difference between attending and declining. Photography Tips for Pets at Weddings Pet photos are often the most shared images from a wedding. Set your photographer up for success: Brief your photographer on the pet timeline so they are ready Schedule dedicated pet portrait time (10 to 15 minutes) Have high-value treats available for attention-getting Use a squeaker toy behind the camera for ear-perked shots Accept candid over posed: the best pet photos happen naturally Get shots of the pet with each partner individually, and together Pro tip: Ask your photographer if they have experience with animals. Some photographers love pet photos and know how to capture them; others find it stressful. If pet photos are a priority, look for a photographer who has them in their portfolio. Cats, Rabbits, and Other Pets Dogs get most of the attention, but other pets can be included too: Cats: Best for getting-ready photos or a brief, controlled appearance. Most cats do not enjoy crowds, so a photo-only role works best. Use a carrier for transport and have a quiet room available. Rabbits: Can appear in outdoor photos. Keep them in a pen or held by the handler. Avoid loud environments. Horses: Popular for rustic or farm weddings. The couple arrives or departs on horseback. Requires a professional handler and venue coordination. For any non-dog pet, prioritize the animal’s comfort over the photo opportunity. A stressed pet does not make for good photos or a good experience. Pet-Inclusive Wedding Checklist Confirm venue pet policy (fees, restrictions, outdoor areas) Book a dedicated pet handler Schedule a vet visit (vaccinations current, health check) Choose pet’s role and attire Test outfit/accessories at home Attend rehearsal with pet Pack a pet day-of kit Brief photographer on pet timeline Communicate pet presence to guests via wedding website Confirm backup/exit plan with handler Arrange post-ceremony pet transport home Share every detail with your guests in one place. Your wedding website is the perfect place to let guests know about your pet’s appearance, share pet photos, collect RSVPs with allergy information , and keep your guest list organized as you plan. Get started free on Joy. Frequently Asked Questions How do you include a dog in your wedding ceremony? The most common way is as a ring bearer or aisle escort. Assign a dedicated handler to walk the dog down the aisle on a leash. Keep the dog’s appearance short (ceremony and photos only) and have the handler take them home before the reception. How much does a wedding pet handler cost? Professional pet attendants for weddings typically charge $150 to $500, depending on hours, travel, and services. Some include grooming, transport, and boarding. A trusted friend or your regular pet sitter can fill this role for less. What flowers are safe for pets at weddings? Roses, sunflowers, snapdragons, zinnias, and orchids are generally safe for dogs and cats. Avoid lilies (toxic to cats), baby’s breath, chrysanthemums, tulips, and daffodils. Always confirm with your florist and vet before putting flowers on your pet. Can you include a cat in your wedding? Yes, but cats typically do best in short, controlled appearances: getting-ready photos or a brief portrait session in a quiet room. Most cats do not enjoy large crowds, loud music, or unfamiliar outdoor spaces. A photo-only role is the safest approach. What if my pet does not cooperate during the ceremony? This is why you need a dedicated handler and a backup plan. If the pet gets anxious, barks, or refuses to walk, the handler quietly removes them. Brief your officiant and wedding party on this plan so everyone stays calm if it happens. The best pet wedding moments are often the unscripted ones.

title: Stagwell Launches Stagwell Curate
body_text: Originally Released On ACCESS Newswire PR Contact Quinn Werner pr@stagwellglobal.com A new AI-powered marketplace and platform designed to reach audiences through premium, trusted media partnerships NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / July 16, 2026 / Stagwell (NASDAQ:STGW), the global challenger network transforming marketing through AI, today announced the launch of Stagwell Curate, a new centralized deal marketplace and bespoke inventory curation platform that consolidates preferred supply relationships across the Stagwell network into a single, always-on source of trusted supply. It is designed to help brands access higher‑quality digital advertising inventory across streaming TV, video, display and audio. Stagwell Curate is part of the Stagwell Media Platform, Stagwell’s team of global media, technology and data investment professionals, and reflects the network’s strategic view that long‑term advantage in programmatic buying is increasingly created on the supply side. The AI-powered platform enables Stagwell to apply its own intelligence, quality standards and performance signals upstream – curating inventory before it ever reaches the bid. The platform provides two key features for clients. The marketplace provides an always‑on, cross‑channel pool of pre‑vetted inventory across CTV, online video, display and audio. Bespoke curation allows brands and agency teams to build customized deal packages aligned to specific audiences, contextual signals, KPIs or sustainability goals. Stagwell Media Platform’s ongoing mission is to improve working media for their clients by partnering with those that can get the bid closer to the impression, whilst not compromising quality. Following the recent launch of The Media Machine , its buying agents will connect directly to Stagwell Curate, giving them instant access to Stagwell’s preferred publisher relationships, pre‑negotiated PMP deals and exclusive pricing when sourcing inventory for every buy. Partners including Freewheel and Magnite will provide access to deep, direct publisher relationships across streaming, video, web and audio. Inventory flowing through the platform is continuously evaluated using log‑level data and supply‑quality models powered by The Trade Desk’s Sincera, delivering enhanced transparency, measurement and accountability. “For years, programmatic innovation has focused on optimizing the bid,” said Matt Adams, Global CEO of Stagwell Media Platform. “As DSP capabilities converge and platforms push buyers toward their own marketplaces, differentiation shifts to supply. Stagwell Curate puts our intelligence above the DSP – allowing us to take a point of view on supply quality, stand behind it with data, and connect it directly to outcomes for clients.” By curating supply closer to the source, Stagwell Curate expands access to premium inventory that traditional DSP‑only optimization may never see, addressing a core limitation of bidder‑side buying, which operates on a partial view of available opportunities. Stagwell Curate is available immediately to clients across the Stagwell network through their existing agency teams, with no DSP migration required. It operates alongside Stagwell Control, the network’s brand safety and media quality offering. Together, the solutions form the Stagwell Supply Product Suite, providing a unified approach to how the network selects, protects and measures the inventory its clients buy. About Stagwell Stagwell is the global challenger network transforming marketing through AI. We deliver scaled creative performance for the world’s most ambitious brands, connecting culture-moving creativity with leading-edge technology to harmonize the art and science of marketing. Led by entrepreneurs, our specialists in 45+ countries are unified under a single purpose: to drive effectiveness and improve business results for our clients. Join us at www.stagwellglobal.com .

Lightbridge will host a conference call on Thursday, August 6, at 4:00 p.m. ET with the investment community to discuss the Company’s financial results and provide an update on its fuel development activities. title: Rio Tinto signs bio pellet supply agreement for Gladstone alumina refineries
body_text: BRISBANE, Australia-- Rio Tinto has signed a five-year offtake agreement with Australian bioenergy company SuperChar Limited (SCL) for the supply of locally produced bio pellets for use at its alumina refineries in Gladstone, with deliveries targeted to commence in 2028. The agreement follows Rio Tinto operational trials and a feasibility study and represents the next stage in assessing the use of bio pellets as one of several potential solutions the company is exploring to reduce reliance on fossil fuels in alumina refining. The trials tested a range of bio pellet and coal blends and demonstrated that bio pellets, under trial conditions, could replace up to 30 per cent of the coal used to generate steam in the refinery boilers. Under the agreement, Rio Tinto plans to undertake a range of operational demonstrations and assessments of bio pellet blends - ranging from 5 to 50 per cent bio pellets - as a supplement to coal used in boilers at its Gladstone alumina refineries¹. This initial offtake agreement with SCL will enable Rio Tinto to further assess the potential role of bio pellets, with scope to increase supply over time if the project is successful. SCL plans to establish a bio pellet production facility in the Gladstone region which will use locally grown bana grass as the feedstock². Bana grass is a high-yielding perennial energy crop suited to Central Queensland. It can be planted and harvested using conventional sugar cane equipment and remains productive for more than 15 years. The facility will initially have capacity to produce 35,000 tonnes of bio pellets a year, and at full contract volumes, could reduce reported Scope 1 emissions by up to 90,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent annually, under Australia’s current National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting framework. Rio Tinto Aluminium Pacific Operations Managing Director Armando Torres said: “Reducing our alumina refineries’ reliance on fossil fuel will require a mix of technologies, innovation and partnerships, and bio pellets are one of the practical options we are exploring as part of that. "The recent trials and feasibility study have given us valuable insights, and this agreement allows us to take the next step in understanding how bio-pellets could work in practice and be scaled for use at our Gladstone operations. "The project also has the potential to support new industries and supply chains in Central Queensland, connecting agriculture and industry in new ways." SCL Executive Chairman Michael Palmer said: "This agreement builds on several years of collaboration and demonstrates the potential for local, regeneratively grown biomass as an alternative industrial fuel, while creating opportunities for regional communities. "We look forward to continuing our partnership with Rio Tinto and progressing the project with local stakeholders." SCL is targeting the progressive roll-out of bana grass planting from late 2026, with the production of bio pellets processing to begin in 2028. 1 Rio Tinto has interests in two alumina refineries in the Gladstone region, Yarwun and Queensland Alumina Ltd. Initial use of SCL's bio pellets is expected to begin at Yarwun, followed by increasing volumes at Queensland Alumina Limited, subject to appropriate approvals and operational readiness at both sites. 2 The establishment of the facility, commencement of production and use of bio pellets at any Rio Tinto Gladstone alumina refineries remains subject to regulatory approvals, and operational readiness.
